key_insight: PAIR-IBD quantified spatial patterns of inflammation and crypt injury that distinguished pathologist-defined active ulcerative colitis from histological remission.
clinical_relevance: The system could complement pathology scoring and clinical-trial histological endpoints, pending further validation.
method: Trained a deep-learning ensemble on three inflammatory bowel disease datasets.
Detected inflammatory cells and segmented mucosal compartments to quantify cell densities and crypt injury.
Compared AI measurements with pathologist-defined disease groups and manual scores.
evidence_signal: In a single clinical network, active biopsies had 5.3-fold higher crypt neutrophil density than Nancy-defined remission, while the strongest reported correlations with manual scores were rs=0.50–0.73.
watch_item: Single-network evaluation limits generalizability; remission-like measurements in inconclusive biopsies do not establish confirmed remission.
paper_title: Spatial AI quantification of inflammatory and architectural features differentiates pathologist-defined active ulcerative colitis from histological remission
